newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bank sale bill fails to clear Romania parliament.
newsitem.headline: Bank sale bill fails to clear Romania parliament.

text.p: A long-awaited Romanian bank privatisation bill failed to clear parliament and will be re-submitted after parliamentary and presidential elections in November, a parliament spokesman said on Wednesday.
The draft law, previously adopted by parliament's upper Senate, was rejected in the lower Chamber of Deputies late on Tuesday lacking a simple majority of 171 votes.

With parliament closing its session on Thursday, the bill -- a target under accords with international lenders -- is expected to be rediscussed when parliament resumes activity after the polls, the spokesman said.

Romania has 34 commercial banks of which six are state-run. Development bank Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare SA (BRD) and farm lender Banca Agricola likely to turn private after legislation has cleared parliament.
Romania should have privatised two of its six state banks last year to meet demands under loan arrangements with the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
The IMF recently warned Romania that failure to carry out structural reforms, including privatisation and restructuring, risked hindering the country's fragile economic recovery.

Under a standby agreement due to expire in April 1997, the IMF had offered Romania some $280 million in loans but withheld loan tranches so far. The Balkan country also expects to draw some $80 million under a World Bank Financial and Enterprise Sector Adjustment Loan (FESAL) by year-end. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
